coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-eight attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 2a66c1c6 at 0444, 14704 bytes, unmoved; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head; required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified and matching their recorded pins; all thirteen recordedInputs files reproduce with basedOn cross-checked against them at zero disagreements. The sharpest attack was carried in from the review I filed immediately before this one. I rejected g18-leftover-join.v2 because its basedOn.inputCorpus.role — 'Named initial states from live exactByteIntent.' — was false of the corpus it pinned. This join carries the byte-identical string, so the temptation was to carry the finding across on the phrasing. Measured instead: g22-input-corpus.v2 carries four initialStates, every one with a stateNamed field and all four distinct, the string exactByteIntent occurs seven times in it, and all four states cite it in their source. Its own whatIsAuthored reads 'Four named initial states drawn from live G22 v1 exactByteIntent'. The claim is true here, so OBL-G22-INPUT-CORPUS at leftoverDesign false has a real basis. The difference between the two cases is worth recording: the G22 chain reached this state by repairing its corpus after I rejected g22-input-corpus.v1 as CLAUDE-G22IC-V1-SF1, and that corpus's own predecessor role records the finding accurately; the G18 chain has not had that repair. Both shortfall tests came back null. platform-tcb-leftover-join.v5 is the DR-126 ledger, pinned and reproducing, and its summary.leftoverDesign is exactly OBL-G22-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-RESERVED-TABLES — the two the join names. G22 v1's leftoverNameNote enumerates four reserved categories, per-OS tables, filesystem selectors, version/build selectors and ikconfigParserVectors, and the join reproduces all four with none dropped. On the dispatch's substantive prohibition I probed structurally rather than counting refusals: twelve probes for glibc, libc., libSystem, ICU, kernel, so.6, .dylib, an ikconfigParserVectors array opener, an allowlist array opener, an x86_64- triple, darwin and manylinux all returned zero, so no library name, path, architecture triple, allowlist or parser vector appears anywhere. Rosetta's four occurrences are all refusals or the 'Never Rosetta' standing. The register checks hold: cell [7] of the DR-G22 row is OPEN and cell [4] is 'Security + release + platform', byte-identical to liveGateOwners and repeated on all four owner-carrying obligations; DR-126's own OPEN token was confirmed separately on the v5 ledger rather than inherited from DR-G22's. The single corpus class contains no semicolon, so it stays one member with its slashes joined, and the join carries exactly one. The successor diff is surgical — five obligations to six, one added and none removed, the FX reason gaining an appended clause with v1's text verbatim as a prefix, doesNot byte-identical at sixteen entries, summary.leftoverDesign unchanged. Predecessor identity is clean on this artifact, and the platform-tcb family it pins now reads a consistent v5/version-5 triple, so the identity defect I filed at v3 is repaired there too. Disclosure: all five Claude-lane verdicts this join pins are mine, including the rejection whose repair it relies on. The risk this cycle was sequence bias in both directions — carrying a fresh finding across on shared phrasing, or carrying three acceptances across on shared shape — and the discriminating measurement separated the cases cleanly. The standards question I raised at G18 remains open and does not bite here, because this corpus names states under any reading.
